turns.user: why are the romanian deadlifts after the squats and not before
turns.reply:
Squats come first because they are the most demanding movement in today's session. They require a massive amount of central nervous system drive, core stability, and raw leg strength. Putting them first when you are completely fresh allows you to lift the heaviest weight with the best possible form. 

Romanian Deadlifts (RDLs) target your posterior chain—your hamstrings and glutes—but they also place a heavy structural load on your lower back and spinal erectors to keep your spine neutral. If you did heavy RDLs first, those lower back muscles would be pre-fatigued, which would make it much harder (and riskier) to keep your torso upright and stable when you get under the barbell for squats. 

By squatting first, we maximize your main strength progression, and then we use the RDLs to specifically overload your hamstrings and glutes once the heavy quad-dominant work is out of the way. 

How does your lower back usually feel by the time you transition from squats to RDLs?
